To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
drip fertigation with weekly fertigation of 1.5kgNha− 1 per week is an efficient and sustainable way to grow okra.

drip fertigated okras with weekly fertilization had the highest yields, N-uptake, intercepted radiation and highest water productivity, and drip fertigation with N–K fertilizers can replace sprinkler irrigation with manure spread.

(i) drip irrigation and fertigation with N–K fertilizers can replace sprinkler irrigation with animal manure in okra production in the Keta sand spit, (ii) fertigation should be done at least once a week to avoid nitrogen leaching, and (iii) drip irrigation can save 30% of irrigation water compared to sprinklers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and sustainable production system of okra in the Keta sand spit, which is characterized by a high water demand and a low soil fertility.
the development of an improved and sustainable production system of okra, based on drip fertigation with weekly N-supply.
the effect of different irrigation and fertilizer management on yield, radiation interception and water use efficiency of okra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drip irrigation with fertigation is a promising alternative to sprinkler irrigation and manure fertilization of okra.
drip fertigation with frequent fertigation is the most efficient and economic method of irrigation for okra production in this sandy soil.
drip fertigation with NPK chemical fertilizers can be used instead of sprinkler irrigation with manure spread or localized manure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
drip fertigation can be used in the Keta sand spit to improve okra production.
drip fertigation of okra with reduced P-supply can substitute sprinkler irrigation and current use of manure.
okra is a promising vegetable for the Keta Sand Spits of Ghana and that drip fertigation is an appropriate method of irrigation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
drip fertigation can be used to improve water and nitrogen use efficiency in okra production in sandy soil.
the current use of sprinklers and animal manure in okra production can be substituted by drip fertigation with a reduced P supply.

drip irrigation with frequent N-fertigation can replace sprinkler irrigation and manure application to okra in the Keta sand Spit, and probably also in other coastal areas with sandy soils and low rainfall.
